name: Electric Blankets
hub_intro: An electric blanket is the cheapest way to stay warm on an Irish winter night: a double underblanket draws 70–120 W, about 3–5 cent an hour at Irish day rates, against 76 cent for a 2 kW heater. You heat the bed you are in, not the whole room. We compare underblankets and heated throws on wattage, controls, size and owner ratings on Amazon.ie.
guide: Heat the person, not the room

A 2 kW heater costs about €0.76 an hour at €0.38/kWh. A double electric underblanket rated 70–120 W costs €0.03–€0.05 an hour at full power, and most people pre-warm the bed and then drop to the lowest setting or switch off. If your goal is a warm bed in a cold bedroom, no heater comes close on running cost.

An underblanket is fitted over the mattress, under the sheet, and warms the bed before you get in. A heated throw goes over you on the sofa or at a desk. Underblankets are the better buy for cold bedrooms; throws are the cheapest way to stay warm while working from home or watching TV without heating the whole house.

Single-control double blankets heat both sides the same. Dual control gives each side its own controller, so one person can run on high while the other stays cool. It usually adds €15–€30 to the price and is worth it for most couples.

Look for overheat protection and an auto shut-off timer, check the blanket fits your mattress size, never use one folded or with a hot-water bottle, and replace it if the wiring feels lumpy or the cord is damaged. Most modern underblankets are machine washable once the controller is detached — check the label first.

faqs.q: How much does an electric blanket cost to run in Ireland?
faqs.a: A double underblanket rated 70–120 W costs €0.027–€0.046 an hour at full power at €0.38/kWh. Eight hours on the highest setting every night would be about €0.21–€0.36; in practice most people pre-warm for 30–60 minutes and run on low or off, so the real cost is a few cent a night.

faqs.q: Is an electric blanket cheaper than a heater?
faqs.a: Yes, by a factor of about 15–25 per hour. A 2 kW heater costs about €0.76 an hour at €0.38/kWh; a double electric blanket costs €0.03–€0.05 at full power. The blanket only warms you and the bed, not the room air, which is exactly why it is so cheap.

faqs.q: Is it safe to leave an electric blanket on all night?
faqs.a: Only if the manufacturer says the model is designed for all-night use on its lowest setting, and many are not. Most include an auto shut-off timer. The safest habit is to pre-warm the bed and switch off, or use the lowest setting with the timer.

faqs.q: Can you wash an electric blanket?
faqs.a: Many modern underblankets and throws are machine washable at 30–40°C once the controller is unplugged and removed. Always check the care label, dry it fully before use, and never tumble dry unless the label allows it.

pages.title: Best Electric Blankets Ireland 2026 (Cost Per Night)
pages.desc: Electric blankets and heated throws on Amazon.ie compared for Irish homes: wattage, cost per hour at Irish rates, dual control and owner ratings.
pages.intro: Heating a bedroom with a 2 kW heater costs about 76 cent an hour. Warming the bed with an electric underblanket costs 3–5 cent. That gap is why electric blankets are the most cost-effective winter buy in Ireland. We compared six underblankets and a heated throw on wattage, controls, size and verified owner ratings on Amazon.ie.

products.name: Cosi Home Double Electric Underblanket (70W)
products.verdict: The Cosi Home double underblanket is the most-reviewed blanket we found on Amazon.ie, with a 4.3-star average from more than 12,000 owners. It covers the basics well: 70 W, three heat settings, a fitted microfleece design and a machine-washable cover. At €0.38/kWh it costs €0.027 an hour on the highest setting, joint-lowest in this guide. The one thing it lacks is dual control, so both sides of the bed run at the same heat. Buy this if you want a proven, low-cost double blanket; pick a dual-control model if you and your partner disagree on temperature.

products.name: Russell Hobbs Dual Control King Underblanket (120W)
cons: Joint-highest wattage in this guide (120 W)
products.verdict: Russell Hobbs' king-size underblanket gives each side of the bed its own detachable controller with three heat settings, which is the feature that ends the 'too hot / too cold' argument for couples. It has a 4.4-star average from more than 1,400 owners on Amazon.ie, is BEAB approved with overheat protection, and machine washes at 40°C once the controls are off. At 120 W it's joint-highest in this guide, which still works out at €0.046 an hour flat out at €0.38/kWh. Buy this if you share the bed and want separate heat; skip it if you sleep alone, where a single-control blanket does the same job for less.

products.name: Warmer Double Electric Blanket, Dual Zones, 9 Settings (120W)
products.verdict: If you want fine control, the Warmer double gives each side nine heat settings and its own timer, with a 4.3-star average from about 1,500 owners. It shares the highest wattage in this guide, 120 W, which still works out at only €0.046 an hour flat out at €0.38/kWh. The extra settings matter most for people who run warm and want something between 'off' and 'low'. Buy it for precise dual-zone control; the Russell Hobbs king-size is the simpler dual-control alternative.

products.name: Daewoo Double Electric Blanket, 3 Heat Settings (85W)
products.verdict: Daewoo's double blanket is the value pick: about €34, 85 W, three settings, overheat protection and a detachable controller so it can be washed. More than 2,000 owners give it a 4.2-star average on Amazon.ie. At €0.38/kWh it costs €0.032 an hour on high. It is thinner than the premium fleece models, which some owners notice on very cold nights. Buy it if price comes first; spend more for dual control or a thicker fleece.

products.name: STATUS Double Electric Underblanket (70W)
cons: Lowest owner rating in this guide (4.0)
products.verdict: At under €30 and 70 W, the STATUS double underblanket is the cheapest to buy and joint-cheapest to run in this guide: €0.027 an hour at full power at €0.38/kWh. It is a basic tie-on underblanket with three settings, and its 4.0-star average from about 1,400 owners is the lowest here. Buy it for a spare room or as a first try of an electric blanket; for nightly use in your main bed, the Cosi Home is the better long-term buy for about €16 more.

products.name: Wärmer Fully Fitted Double Electric Blanket, Dual Control (120W)
pros: Dual control, 3 heat settings per side
cons: Joint-highest wattage in this guide (120 W)
products.verdict: Wärmer's fully fitted double blanket has the highest owner rating in this guide, 4.5 stars from more than 2,300 people on Amazon.ie. It goes on like a fitted sheet, with a 40 cm elasticated skirt that stops it sliding around, and each side has its own detachable controller with three heat settings. At about €72 it is the most expensive here, and at 120 W it costs €0.046 an hour flat out at €0.38/kWh. Buy it if you want the best-reviewed blanket that stays put on the mattress; the Russell Hobbs king-size gives dual control for about €20 less.

products.name: Bauer Professional Electric Heated Throw, 120 x 160 cm
pros: For the sofa or desk, not just bed
cons: Wattage not published on the listing
products.verdict: The Bauer heated throw is for the hours you are not in bed: on the sofa or at a desk while working from home. It is a 120 x 160 cm fleece throw with a 4.4-star average from more than 300 owners. The listing does not state its wattage, so we do not quote an hourly cost, but heated throws as a type draw a small fraction of what any room heater does. Buy it to stay warm in one spot without heating the whole house; for the bed, choose an underblanket above.
